body:
Working entry (`chk-i5hwelaf`, Epoch 4 — Inside the canvas): «Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes — each circle a
node, its draw commands grouped by it, with stand checks (v040-10, v040-11)», with seven CARRYs folded below.

- Circle Drawer's canvas widget (`CircleCanvas` in `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs`) declares one
  virtual node per circle it paints through `Widget::virtual_nodes`: an author key, an AccessKit role, a non-empty name
  and a region in its content box. Circle Drawer becomes the first served app to declare virtual nodes, so each circle
  reads as a node — `{owner}///{key}` — in the accessibility tree, the snapshot, the diff, the UI graph, `actions`,
  `layout` and exploration, as the three earlier chunks built them on fixture canvases.

- `click` on a circle's node acts on its circle and its diff names it; a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed
  circle node is refused with that cause (v040-11's acceptance, on the stand).

- The canvas reading (`Session::canvas`, the `canvas` verb) groups a canvas's draw commands under the virtual node that
  covers them (v040-10's last open clause), and a changed command reads with an identity in the reading's diff (CARRY 1).
- Stand checks in both layout modes, and the binary-level reading of a virtual node's id and name (CARRY 4).
- Keyboard reach of the circles is «Canvas keyboard path»'s, the next entry — not built here.
- A rotated or scaled canvas's virtual nodes are «Pan and zoom»'s (its own CARRY) — not built here.

- The lint's label-overlap, label-contrast, command-outside-region and zero-area-shape readings stay their residuals'
  (res-zahb4t5s, res-afru4fnu, res-6djljwev, res-5aosveco) unless a CARRY below takes one.

alone, test-plan `amd-nasxjktn`).

How costs were measured: file and line reads at HEAD `a5d18f604`; the code-graph impact query (trace
`tree-query-2026-11-25-circle-drawer-virtual-nodes.json`, 59 rows); `stand_canvas_commands`' committed table; and the
fixture's circle sequence (`session_common::circles`) replayed off-tree for a 700 × 400 content box — at 12 circles 0
spill the box, 1 is under 16 px, 2 overlapping pairs, 2 centres under a later disc; at 100 circles 3 spill, 5 under
14 px, 7 under 16 px, 11 under 18 px, 109 overlapping pairs, 26 centres under a later disc. A size marked *derived* is
arithmetic on committed numbers, not a run.

---

## F1 — What a click on a circle's node does (v040-11 «a click on one acts on its circle and its diff names it»)

**Today.** `CircleDrawer`'s `onclick` (`circle_drawer.rs:267`) always pushes a new circle at the click point. The driver
acts on a virtual node at its region's centre (`execute.rs:794`). So a click on a circle's node adds a second circle on
top of it, and the diff names the new node, never the clicked one.

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** The stand app's behaviour; under B1 also the widget declaration's form
(`Widget::virtual_nodes`, `VirtualNodeDeclaration`, blitz-dom behind `custom-widget`, an escher addition). A selected
state crosses as the snapshot's existing closed `selected` reading — a closed value inside a ratified carrier, no
widening by the 2026-10-10 rule. The declaration's form was the delegate's F2 A (PROVISIONAL); its one added field so far,
`disabled`, was the founder's own F8 A.

| Option | What it does | Measured cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | App unchanged: a click on a circle's node adds a circle at its centre | 0 lines. v040-11's click clause stays unmet with no later owner: «Canvas keyboard path» claims v040-11 and inherits it |
| B1 | 7GUIs selection: a click inside a circle selects it (painted filled), adds none; `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `selected`, written to the tree, read as the snapshot's `selected` | blitz-dom `custom_widget.rs` +1 field and doc; `dioxus_document.rs` +3 lines (`:416`); the 8 declaration literals in 4 files (`custom_widget.rs`, `virtual_node.rs`, `fixtures/mod.rs`, `virtual_nodes_declared.rs`) take `selected: false`; app: a selection signal and its declared writes; the diff names the node, `differs: [selected]` |
| B2 | 7GUIs selection as B1, the state carried in the declared name («Circle 3, 40 px, selected») | app only; the diff names the node, `differs: [name]`; a state read from a name, not a state field — what an assistive technology hears is the name |
| C | A click on a circle opens its diameter dialog (today's double click) | app only; the diff names the dialog's nodes, not the circle — the clause stays unmet |

**Dependences.** F4: under B1/B2 a click on a circle another circle covers would select the top one, so F4 B makes that
refusal honest. F2/F3: selection repaints a fill, so a selected circle's commands change — CARRY 1's identity question.
`GRAPH_DRIVES` (`tests/common/mod.rs:352-360`): its double click lands on the circle its first drive added, so under
B1/B2 that first click of the pair selects rather than adds — the drives are re-read.

**Whose.** B1 — the founder's (the declaration's form, the class of F8 A). A, B2, C — the operator's (a stand change, no
engine change and no crossing).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A (the entry asks each circle a node, not a click semantics).

## F2 — The canvas answer grouped by virtual node (v040-10 «the commands grouped under the virtual node that covers them»; CARRY 1 «a changed command has no identity»)

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** security-plan `decision/virtual-node-crossing` (ratified): «the lint and canvas

rule — and the playbook's `rul-izni57qv` (Boundary widening) escalates it. Rows reached by name: security-plan
`decision/virtual-node-crossing`, `decision/canvas-content-crossing`, `decision/kept-check-canvas-answer`,

`decision/canvas-reading-diffable`, `decision/kept-check-never-logged`, `contract/command-span/never-fielded`;

`decision/canvas-line-form-conventions` (the line form). Read as not reached: the snapshot, graph, actions and layout
rows (their carriers do not change).

**The shared mechanism (every option but A).** A command belongs to the last-declared taken node whose region holds the
centre of the command's bounds (declaration order read as paint order, a stated assumption); a layer push or pop, or a
command whose centre no region holds, belongs to none. A label is painted after every circle (`circle_drawer.rs:175`),

| D | The node's id `{owner}///{key}` | as B plus the id; *derived* ~24 B a line ≈ 7 KB, 6 parts may become 7; the same class the founder ratified for graph, actions and layout (F13 A) |
